.github/workflows/ci.yml.text:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

# Serialize per-ref so overlapping runs don't step on each other (especially the
# live job, which mutates a shared pfSense box). We never cancel the in-flight
# run — a half-finished live test can leave a throwaway alias behind.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Hermetic build + unit tests. Runs on GitHub-hosted runners for every push
  # and pull request. Never talks to a real pfSense box: the live acceptance
  # tests self-skip here because TF_ACC is unset, so only the mock-backed tests
  # in internal/provider run.
  hermetic:
    name: Build + unit tests (hermetic)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: '1.26.6'
          cache: true
      - name: gofmt (must be clean)
        run: test -z "$(gofmt -l .)"
      - name: go vet
        run: go vet ./...
      - name: go build
        run: go build ./...
      - name: go test (mock-backed)
        run: go test ./...

  # Live acceptance tests against the real pfSense box, on the self-hosted
  # runner (the `pfsense-runner` custom app on the NAS). These tests mutate the
  # box (create/update/import/destroy a throwaway alias), so the job is opt-in:
  # manual `workflow_dispatch` or a post-merge push to main only.
  #
  # SECURITY: a self-hosted runner executes the repo's code. It must therefore
  # NEVER run on `pull_request` — otherwise anyone who opens a PR against this
  # public repo could run arbitrary code on the NAS. Keeping it to dispatch +
  # push-to-main means only maintainers with write access can reach it.
  live:
    name: Live acceptance tests (pfSense)
    runs-on: [self-hosted, pfsense]
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
    env:
      TF_ACC: '1'
      PFSENSE_URL: ${{ secrets.PFSENSE_URL }}
      PFSENSE_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.PFSENSE_USERNAME }}
      PFSENSE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PFSENSE_PASSWORD }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: '1.26.6'
          cache: true
      - name: go test (live, TF_ACC)
        # TF_ACC=1 flips the live acceptance tests on; the mock-backed tests
        # also run but are unaffected (they never consult TF_ACC). Equivalent to
        # `make testacc`, so any live test the repo adds is picked up regardless
        # of its name.
        run: go test ./... -v -timeout 120m

.github/workflows/release.yml.text:
name: release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  goreleaser:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: 'go.mod'
          cache: true

      # Import the signing key into the runner's keyring. The `signs`
      # block in .goreleaser.yml signs SHA256SUMS with the key selected
      # by GPG_FINGERPRINT; without this import gpg fails with
      # "skipped ...: No secret key". Same action the v0.0.x workflow used.
      - name: Import GPG key
        uses: crazy-max/ghaction-import-gpg@v6
        with:
          gpg_private_key: ${{ secrets.GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          passphrase: ${{ secrets.PASSPHRASE }}

      # GoReleaser >= 2.6 is required: .goreleaser.yml uses the
      # `archives.formats` list form. `latest` resolves to a current 2.x.
      - uses: goreleaser/goreleaser-action@v6
        with:
          distribution: goreleaser
          version: latest
          args: release --clean
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # Required by the `signs` block in .goreleaser.yml; the key
          # itself is imported by the step above.
          GPG_FINGERPRINT: ${{ secrets.GPG_FINGERPRINT }}
